headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist because transformers can read/write files and use broad network egress while LlamaFactory is a local, non-I/O agent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no filesystem, clipboard, stdin/stdout, or MCP surfaces, so it cannot ingest B’s outputs by default. B can read/write files and use stdin/stdout, so a manual copy-paste or file bridge could carry injected text into A, but that requires unusual operator setup and the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies B output into A as training or prompt text, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared file is introduced between the agents, B can place attacker-controlled content for A to consume.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not copy B outputs into A without review.
Disable shared folders between the two processes.
Use a fixed prompt template for A that strips instructions from pasted text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B can read and write files and has broad network egress, while A is non-networked and touches no data classes. If both are pointed at the same workspace, B can exfiltrate whatever A’s artifacts contain; A itself does not leak, but the pair creates a default shared-workspace leakage path.
conditions: IF A and B share a writable directory, B can read A-produced artifacts.
IF those artifacts contain sensitive content, B can transmit them over its broad network egress.
mitigations: Place A and B in separate directories.
Mount A’s output directory read-only for B.
Block B’s outbound network except to approved endpoints.
Review generated files before B processes them.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A cannot write files, modify git, or use subprocesses, so it cannot contend for mutable resources with B. B can write files and spawn subprocesses, but without overlapping write surfaces or shared mutable state, the conflict pathway is weak and mostly limited to accidental overwrite if an operator creates one.
conditions: IF the operator maps both agents to the same writable directory, B may overwrite A’s artifacts.
IF a shared git repository is introduced externally, B can mutate state that A cannot coordinate on.
mitigations: Use distinct output directories.
Avoid sharing a git checkout between the agents.
Run B with a dedicated service account.
Add file-locking around any shared artifact path.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a fine-tuning framework and B is a document-processing stack; if A’s generated text or model artifacts are fed into B, B can treat them as authoritative inputs and transform them without verification. B’s file and API surfaces make downstream action easy, so the pair can amplify errors even though A itself is not an action-taking agent.
conditions: IF A-generated outputs are piped into B without validation, B can propagate incorrect facts.
IF B is configured to publish or serve processed results, those errors can reach downstream consumers.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between A and B.
Validate A outputs against a schema before B consumes them.
Disable automatic publishing in B.
Log provenance for any A-derived inputs.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only open-source tools with no declared secrets, OAuth scopes, or regulated data classes, so there is no direct residency or certification mismatch evidenced here. The only compliance concern is operational: if the operator feeds regulated data into B’s broad file/network surfaces, that would be a deployment choice rather than a documented pairwise violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through B’s networked environment, residency or retention controls may be required.
IF the operator stores sensitive artifacts in shared files, local policy may be implicated.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace.
Confirm retention settings before processing sensitive files.
Use a local-only deployment for sensitive workloads.
Document the data flow before enabling B’s network access.
